title: Anthropic opens Claude computer use beta to Team and Enterprise plans
subtitle: Claude can see the screen and act in allow-listed desktop apps on Team and Enterprise, with admin policy keys, off-by-default enablement and gradual rollout.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Anthropic's November 20 release notes add Claude computer use as a beta on Team and Enterprise plans, available in the new Claude experience in Claude Desktop and from Claude on the web and mobile when Computer access is on. The feature lets Claude see a user's screen and act in the desktop apps they allow. It is off by default on both tiers; enablement depends on the organization's Computer use setting, the user's role on Enterprise plans and each user's own switch. Admins can hard-lock it off on a given machine with the Claude Desktop policy key computerUseEnabled set to false.

This is not new capability — Claude's computer-use research preview has been running for more than a year — but it is the first time Anthropic has shipped it to Team and Enterprise with the controls those customers require. Allow lists, admin policy keys and off-by-default posture are the three features corporate security teams actually care about, and the bet is that controlled access to an agent that drives SaaS apps and desktop tools is worth more to buyers than a demo-quality preview with no governance.

The timing is not coincidence. Google shipped Gemini computer use on Mac in the same week, with similar mitigations — isolated window, per-action confirmation, prompt-injection warnings. The two labs are competing on the same product on the same calendar. For buyers, that is good news: parallel rollouts mean parallel security audits, and the lessons from one vendor's incidents will shape the controls on the other's.

A note for learners: the enterprise controls are where this feature will succeed or fail. Allow lists tell the agent which apps it may touch; policy keys let admins ship machines with the capability disabled; role-based enablement keeps it off interns' accounts. If you're in IT and someone asks you to turn Claude computer use on, start by writing down the three apps it may act in, the one user who gets access, and the incident-response path when something goes wrong. That document is the real deployment, not the switch.
